subject: BF0ECD50DBFC42C3A855CE24E0DCAABD
introduction: Four short passages: a question to ‘Abdu’l-Bahá about whether all games are forbidden (no, innocent ones pursued for recreation are not), his remark that the wise look at the end of a thing, not its first pleasure, and two statements of the prohibition, one from the Báb and one from the Kitáb-i-Aqdas. The Qur’an forbade games of chance together with wine in two steps, first weighing their harm against their use and then calling them Satan’s handiwork; Proverbs warns the one who “maketh haste to be rich”.
questions: Where does recreation end and gambling begin?
Reading 2 judges a pleasure by its consequences. Is that how you decide what to avoid?
Why might gambling be forbidden together with wine and opium?

outside.why: Some games are innocent recreation. To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.
The wise look to consequences, not beginnings. He that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent.
The reading follows this verse: strong drink and games of chance and idols and divining arrows are only an infamy of Satan’s handiwork.

Forbidden with opium. The Qur’an’s earlier verse reasons before it forbids: in both is great sin, and some utility for men; but the sin of them is greater than their usefulness. What utility might be meant, and how does reading 2 weigh it?
